| 330 | **`--bundle-seams`: detect module boundaries in bundled JS**: Minified bundles (claude-code's cli.js, mermaid.min.js, etc.) wrap each original source module in a compact helper pattern — for esbuild it's `var X = E(() => { ... });`, for webpack `__webpack_modules__ = { N: (module, exports, require) => ... }`, Rollup has its own, Parcel has its own, etc. Each wrapper call marks the seam between two original source files from before bundling. Feature: (a) auto-detect which wrapper pattern is in use by scanning for the most-frequent recurring structure, (b) list every wrapper with its line range and first 1-3 non-blank lines as a preview, (c) optionally correlate with string literals inside each module body to guess at original source paths (bundles often leak `// node_modules/foo/bar.js` as comments or paths inside error-message strings). On claude-code's 513k-line cli.js this would produce a rough architectural map — you'd see which chunk is lodash, which is zod, which is claude-code-proper, which is telemetry — without needing to run the bundle or rely on `--extensions` scanning. Natural companion to `--file-bookends` (#n/a, landed 2c5145e) which already surfaces top/tail entry points. Foundation for making #329 analysis context include "which bundled module is this function from?" and for architectural discovery work on any minified bundle. Depends on: #313 (minified-JS detection/prettification). Related: #327 (template literal interpolation resolution), #329 (pre-summarized LLM analysis context). | **design needed, depends on #313** |

[^130h]: **Fan-out/fan-in metrics** — Functions with high fan-out (call many diverse in-index functions) are likely orchestrators / control centers. Even if called only once, a function that calls `buildIndex`, `parseFunctions`, `writeInvertedIndex`, and `buildFunctionIndex` is clearly coordinating something important. Score: `fan_out x log(fan_in + 1)` finds the sweet spot between "calls lots of things" and "is itself called by several things." Functions that appear as intermediate nodes in many call trees (not leaves, not roots) are the connective tissue. Data available via `findCallees` (fan-out) and `findCallers` (fan-in).

[^130i]: **PageRank-style / Hub Functions scoring** — Current metrics all fail to surface what's semantically important: Most Called is swamped by stdlib (`slice`, `push`, `trim`). Even with `--defined-only`, utility functions (`errorResponse`, `jsonResponse`) dominate. Hotspots weights by size x calls but still catches plumbing. Domain Functions uses TF-IDF naming rarity but that's about naming, not structural importance. What's needed: recursive importance scoring where a function's importance is boosted by the importance of its callers (PageRank on the call graph). The data exists in `getCallInventory`'s in-index caller lists — needs iterative scoring over that graph. Key insight: frequency-based metrics find plumbing; structural-centrality metrics find architecture.

[^329]: **Pre-summarized LLM analysis — design notes.** Problem: local 4B models can't meaningfully analyze 1000+ line functions — they latch onto the first few lines and produce useless output. Even Claude's analysis of masked code, while good, misses the architectural "so what" (e.g. identifies all the config parsing but not that the function's purpose is to bridge user input to the agentic loop). **Solution**: Before sending code to the LLM, CodeExam pre-digests its own analysis into a structured context block. Example prompt for a local LLM analyzing the 1200-line `GCz` function:

> Analyze this CLI entry point function (1,200 lines). Here's what we already know:
> - Contains 78 CLI options (--debug, --print, --model, --resume, etc.)
> - Is the run() function called from main(), breadcrumb "run_function_start"
> - Calls: setup(), showSetupScreens(), REPL component, runHeadless()
> - Has 3 modes: interactive (REPL), print (headless), resume (restore session)
> - Key decisions: permission mode, MCP config, thinking config, model selection
>
> Source code of the first 200 lines: [code]
>
> What does this function do and what are its most important behaviors?

**What CodeExam contributes to the prompt** (all already available): (1) Command catalog → CLI options count and key flags. (2) Breadcrumbs → which phase this function belongs to. (3) Callees → what functions it calls (high-level architecture). (4) Entry points → whether this is a root function or called from elsewhere. (5) Rename map → meaningful names for obfuscated callees. **Implementation**: New `buildAnalysisContext(funcName)` method that assembles these into a structured preamble. The LLM prompt becomes: preamble (200-400 tokens of structured context) + truncated source (200-500 lines) + question. This fits comfortably in a 2K-4K context window while giving the LLM enough scaffolding to reason about architecture, not just syntax. **Key insight**: CodeExam's static analysis compensates for the local LLM's limited reasoning — the LLM adds natural language synthesis that CodeExam can't do.

[^254b]: **"What should I look at first?"** — The goal: when a user opens an index of unfamiliar code, surface the 5-10 functions/classes that a senior engineer would tell a new team member to read first. Current approaches and why they fall short: (1) Most Called — swamped by external/stdlib. (2) Most Called --defined-only — surfaces utility functions, not domain logic. (3) Hotspots — same problem, weighted by size. (4) Domain Functions — TF-IDF on naming is about rarity, not importance. (5) Vocabulary — good for learning nomenclature but doesn't point to specific code. Two promising new angles: **(a) Fan-out scoring**: functions that call many diverse in-index targets are orchestrators (see #130h). **(b) UI-structure analysis**: look at the UI definition layer (HTML templates, route tables, CLI arg parsers, menu definitions, event handlers) to extract the "vocabulary of user-facing actions." These are curated by humans and represent intentional feature boundaries. The functions wired to UI elements are likely entry points into important domain logic. For web apps: route handlers; for CLI tools: argparse options; for GUI apps: menu items and dialog handlers. Could be implemented as a heuristic that identifies UI-definition patterns and boosts the importance of functions referenced from them.

| 332 | **Rename map enrichment from esbuild `__name` helper calls**: esbuild bundles compiled with `--keep-names` (default for many configs) preserve original function names as string-literal arguments to a generated `__name` helper. The helper is typically `var o = (t, e) => Object.defineProperty(t, "name", { value: e, configurable: true });` (mermaid) or similar — detectable by shape. Every `o(NAME, "originalName")` call is then a **ground-truth pair**: the obfuscated identifier NAME is the function originally called "originalName". This is a *much* higher-confidence rename source than the keyword-extraction heuristic in #3 because it's the actual original name preserved by the bundler, not an inference. Implementation: (a) add a fourth helper-shape detector to bundle-seams' `_detectBundleHelpers` that recognizes the `__name` shape (calls `Object.defineProperty(_, "name", ...)`), (b) new rename-map pass that scans for `<nameHelper>(IDENT, "STRING")` patterns and creates `IDENT → IDENT_NAME_STRING` entries, (c) priority: should override `_KW_` (lower confidence) but defer to `_CMD_` (higher specificity). Tier ranking: `_CMD_` > `_NAME_` > `_IMPORT_` > `_KW_`. Estimated impact on mermaid.min.js: hundreds of high-quality renames replacing keyword guesses (e.g. `IW → IW_NAME_MERGE_ICON_TRANSFORMATIONS` instead of whatever `_KW_` came up with). Also valuable on any other esbuild bundle compiled with `--keep-names`. Surfaced by --bundle-seams GUI inspection on mermaid; the user noticed `o(g_e, "attrRemove")`-style entries align directly with the underlying functions. | **planned, important, depends on #330** |

| 357 | **Prompt-catalog: detect ternary-assembled prompts**: Current detector sees each string literal in isolation. Code like `const prompt = isMasked ? "variant A text…" : "variant B text…"` — or the 3-way form `cond1 ? "…" : cond2 ? "…" : "…"` used in CodeExam's own claim.js — produces one catalog entry PER branch, each holding only partial text. Filter/search for text that spans branches (e.g. `"TASK: For each element/limitation in the patent claim, categorize how this file relates to it using EXACTLY one of these labels:"` where the label list is itself a ternary interpolation) finds nothing, because no single entry contains the composite. **Fix**: when a string-literal match is a branch of a `ternary_expression` (tree-sitter JS node type) or an operand of a `+` concatenation chain, or a `${…}` interpolation inside a template literal, walk up to the enclosing expression and collect ALL sibling branches into ONE catalog entry with visible separators. Preferred approach uses tree-sitter since ternaries across quote boundaries get brittle with regex. Same logic should apply to simple `+` concatenation (`"prefix" + name + " suffix"`) and template literals with conditional interpolations. Surfaced 2026-04-24 during prompt-catalog testing on CodeExam's own claim.js source — screenshot shows top-pane prompt truncated vs. full text visible in lower-pane source. | **planned, medium** |
| 356 | **Depth-aware "Break Long Lines" prettifier**: Current `prettifyLongLine()` in `public/app.js` uses regex substitutions to insert breaks after `),`, `;`, and `,name=function/arrow` in lines >300 chars. Works well for most cli.js blocks but treats all `),` the same. Fails when the enclosing call has a trailing argument after a nested call, e.g. `IG8_KW_CACHE_BREAK_COMPUTE("output_style", () => Up9_KW_STYLE_OUTPUT(_), "User can change output style mid-session...")` — the `)` closing the nested `Up9_...(_)` call is followed by `,` + the description string, so the current rule splits the description onto its own line even though it's part of the same outer call. **Fix**: rewrite as a small state machine that tracks paren/bracket depth (and string/template/comment state so it doesn't miscount depth from `(` inside a string). Rule becomes: break at `,` whose enclosing depth equals the line's minimum depth. Example: in `j=[pt(a,b),pt(c,d),IG8(e,f,g)]`, minDepth=1 (inside `[`), breaks only at depth-1 commas — between sibling entries, not inside `IG8(...)`'s args. **Size**: ~40 lines. **Files**: `public/app.js` `prettifyLongLine`. Surfaced 2026-04-24 during article screenshot polishing, after user flagged inner-call commas being mistakenly broken. | **planned, small** |

| 348 | **Parser mis-captures TypeScript-compiled private-field initializers as a function name**: When TypeScript compiles `class X { #field1 = ...; #field2 = ...; method() {...} }` to older JS targets, the private fields become `WeakMap`-based polyfills in a single computed-key initializer at the top of the class body: `class X { [(_X_field1 = new WeakMap(), _X_field2 = new WeakMap(), ..., _X_methodImpl = function() {...}, ..., _X_instances = new WeakSet())] }`. Our regex function parser sees the computed-key `[...]` and treats the entire expression — hundreds of lines of JS including complete function bodies — as ONE method name. Example: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/lib/BetaMessageStream.js` produces a "method" named `[(_BetaMessageStream_currentMessageSnapshot = new WeakMap(), ... _BetaMessageStream_getFinalMessage = function() { if (this.receivedMessages.length === 0) { throw new error_1.AnthropicError(...) } ... }, ... )]` spanning L342-L611 (270 lines). Effects: (a) --list-functions dumps kilobytes of JS into the listing display [mitigated 2026-04-15 by clamping display to 80 chars], (b) the real methods inside the polyfilled initializer (e.g. `_BetaMessageStream_getFinalMessage`, `_BetaMessageStream_accumulateMessage`) don't appear as separate entries in the function index so they can't be clicked/analyzed individually, (c) the fingerprint / struct-dupe analysis treats the whole blob as one function. Fix: detect the TS-compiled computed-key pattern (`class X { [(...)]` followed by `WeakMap()` / `WeakSet()` / `function` within the `[...]`) and split it into individual method entries. Tree-sitter may already get this right — worth verifying and if so adjusting the hybrid-merge priority. Surfaced 2026-04-15 during Franken_AI_SDK inspection. | **planned, medium** |

Must be explicitly opt-in, never on by default, and gated behind the `--air-gapped` mode declaration from #295. **Robots / consent**: should fetch and respect `robots.txt` (or at least surface its content to the user before proceeding); for a "polite" default, also obey `Crawl-delay` and present the target hostname for confirmation before any request. **Scope discipline**: same-origin only by default — don't recursively follow links to other hosts. Pairs with #333 (webpack / Parcel detection) since most modern web apps will produce bundled output that needs the broader pattern detector to be useful. | **planned, design needed, depends on #295 (air-gapped mode)** |
| 333 | **`--bundle-seams`: detect webpack / Parcel / Rollup / Vite bundle patterns**: Current `--bundle-seams` only recognizes esbuild's lazy-factory wrapper shape (`E(() => {...})` and `C(() => {...})`). claude.ai's bundles produced no detection on first try, almost certainly because the site is built with webpack (or a Next.js fork variant). Each major bundler uses a distinct module-wrapper convention; detection is mechanical once the patterns are characterized. Patterns to add: **(a) webpack array form** — `(function(modules){...})([function(module,exports,__webpack_require__){...}, function(...){...}, ...])` with numeric module IDs; **(b) webpack object form** (modern, more common) — `__webpack_modules__ = { "./src/foo.js": (__unused_webpack_module, __webpack_exports__, __webpack_require__) => {...}, "./src/bar.tsx": ... }` — **the object keys are literal source-file paths**, which is gold: zero heuristics needed for source identification, just parse the keys; **(c) Parcel** — `parcelRequire["<hash>"] = function(require, module) {...}`; **(d) Rollup** (ESM output) — typically flat scope with no per-module wrappers, so the fallback is function-proximity grouping (similar to the gap-module approach added for esbuild-iife); **(e) Vite (prod)** — usually Rollup output, same limitation as (d). Webpack object form should be the highest-priority addition because it provides original source paths for free and webpack is the most prevalent web bundler. Surfaced by --bundle-seams testing on claude.ai bundles which produced no matches under the esbuild detector. | **planned, important, depends on #330** |
| 308 | **CSS indexing and cross-file correlation**: CSS files load in CLI without `--extensions` but not in GUI Build Index. Investigate: (a) CSS doesn't contain function definitions, but can it reference JS functions (e.g. in `url()`, custom properties, or animation names)? (b) Test loading CSS alongside JS and check whether any CSS→JS references get correlated in callers/call graph. (c) Ensure GUI Build Index includes CSS if CLI does. | **research** |
| 309 | **False function-name highlighting in HTML/CSS**: CSS files: skip linkification entirely. HTML files: only linkify inside `<script>` blocks. Commit e0bb544. | done |
| 310 | **HTML↔JS ID cross-referencing**: In HTML files, element IDs (e.g. `id="fs-save-png"`) should be correlated with JS references to those IDs (e.g. `$('#fs-save-png')`). Show the connection in callers/callees or a new "references" view. | **design needed** |
| 311 | **Event-driven function call detection**: Added regex for `addEventListener`/`.on()`/`.once()` with named handler callbacks in both `findCallees()` (call_type `event-handler`) and `getCallCounts()`. Arrow callbacks like `() => doSomething()` — the inner call is already caught by existing patterns. Commit e0bb544. Remaining: audit Entry Points/Gaps implications, jQuery `.on()` with object syntax. | **partially done** |
| 312 | **CSS class ↔ JS correlation**: CSS class selectors (e.g. `.src-fn-link { ... }`) should be correlated with JS that references them (e.g. `span.className = 'src-fn-link'`). This is a cross-language string-based reference, not a function call, but valuable for understanding UI wiring. Related to #310 (HTML↔JS IDs). | **design needed** |
| 313 | **Minified JS: prettifier/deobfuscator**: js-beautify integrated — detects `.min.js` or JS/CSS with very long avg lines, prettifies before indexing. Commit e0bb544. Deobfuscation research: **webcrack** (npm, JS-native, webpack bundles), **wakaru** (JS-native), or local LLM for name recovery (#200/#293). | **done (js-beautify), research (deobfuscation)** |
